findings.area: same-host cancellation versus retry of retained NT cleanup
findings.problem: status_resource_done records that the retired model/control permission obligation has completed; it does not prove this invocation detached the remaining NT cell. If model_ready is false, the worker skips lines75-92 and leaves host->status_cell attached, but lines98-109 still run whenever status_resource_done is true. The local cell is still NULL and closed is only its default STATUS_SUCCESS. A retained NT owner is then asserted absent or overwritten with NULL and may be unregistered without an actual close.
concrete_schedule: A retired host reaches actual HostSAFE with controls/jobs/physical retirement drained. The worker sets status_resource_done=true and decrements host_resources_pending, detaches the cell and performs actual NT cleanup. That close/unmap fails and leaves an exact partial cell owner; the worker restores host->status_cell and requeues it. host_status_owners remains1, as intended.

A fresh CANCEL is admitted through the still-registered exact host/producer identity. It owns its independent producer request pin and increments host->status_controls. Pause it after its lock release at line269, before decrementing that control at line273.

A recovery worker pops the queued host and sets status_busy. host_status_model_ready_locked is false because status_controls is nonzero, so it performs no detach/NT close; its local cell remains NULL and local closed remains the default success value.

The worker reacquires remote_lock and enters the unconditional status_resource_done block. Debug builds fail assert(!host->status_cell). With NDEBUG, host->status_cell=cell overwrites the real retained cell with NULL. If not requeued meanwhile, the registry owner and host_status_owners count are immediately removed; if a queue exists, a later pass can remove them after the pointer has already been lost.

The original section/view/heap cell owner is now unreachable. CANCEL eventually drops its request/control pins, permitting whole-producer finalization with both host counters0 despite the abandoned real NT resource. The new !status_queued test does not protect the preceding pointer overwrite.
findings.impact: A supported real NT-cleanup failure followed by a legitimate concurrent retired-host CANCEL can abort debug execution or lose NT ownership and falsely satisfy the stronger whole-producer cleanup condition in release builds. This is a source-level interleaving, not an observed failure.
findings.minimal_fix: Track whether this specific invocation actually took ownership of host->status_cell (including a deliberately proven empty owner path), and run the reattach/close-completion/unregister block only for that owned path. If readiness is blocked by a control, leave the attached cell untouched and retain/requeue the registry/FIFO owner. Do not treat status_resource_done or a default local success code as proof of an NT close. Keep the queued/busy/partial-owner guards and actual failed-cell restoration; do not suppress the assert or lower producer counters to make the path pass.
findings.acceptance_criterion: After an actual retained host close/unmap failure, hold a real CANCEL control across a worker retry. That retry must not detach, overwrite, uncount or unregister a cell it did not own. Once the control settles, an actual subsequent cleanup must consume the exact NT owner before host_status_owners drops or whole-producer SAFE can finalize. No validation was run.

findings.problem: A newly created producer binds protocol before registry publication, but the existing-producer duplicate branch matches only root/PID/birth/generation and returns its ID without checking current->protocol against the requested protocol. ACQUIRE can therefore report success for a lease incompatible with the request’s version.
concrete_schedule: Acquire an active watched v1 producer for root/PID/birth/generation G.
Send a version2 ACQUIRE for that same identity/G. producer_acquire_protocol finds the v1 current producer and returns its lease with ERROR_SUCCESS.

The returned response still carries version2, but the lease remains correctly bound to protocol1. The first v2 PREPARE then fails the packet_producer_begin protocol check. The symmetric v2-existing/v1-acquire case can similarly return an unusable v1 lease response.
findings.impact: Version negotiation/idempotence is inconsistent at acquisition and can break migration/retry behavior while later controls correctly enforce the bound protocol. This is not an unsafe retagging or a claim of NT ownership loss; it is an erroneous success response at the new version boundary.
findings.minimal_fix: Require current->protocol==protocol before returning an existing lease. Reject a mismatched acquisition with an appropriate explicit error; do not retag or mutate the existing producer and do not broaden v1 admission. Preserve successful same-protocol idempotent acquisition and the existing root/PID/birth/generation identity checks.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Same-identity repeated acquisition succeeds only for the same bound protocol. A v1/v2 mismatch returns no lease success and leaves the existing producer/version/resources unchanged. No test was executed.

reviews.verdict: One P1 and one P2 block source admission. A retained host NT cell can be overwritten/lost under NDEBUG when a later retry skips detachment because CANCEL holds a control, yet resource_done still enters the unconditional close-completion block. The idempotent producer-acquire lookup also returns an existing lease without matching its bound protocol. Keep the conservative host/model fence, all-zero host sequences and stronger producer counters when fixing these issues.
